title: Text AI: a small language model in the FPGA writes text letter by letter
summary: A language model, the idea behind chatbots, made small enough for the FPGA: it reads the last 16 letters and scores every letter that could come next, 64 multiplications per clock. Give it the start of a sentence and watch it write on, choose how adventurous it is, see what it was thinking, and train it on your own text.

slots.1: General neural network engine (up to 4 layers, 64 multiplications per clock)

parts: nothing: everything happens inside the FPGA
tested: the self-test passed 8 of 8 checks on the real board (October 2026): random networks and the text model equal to the Python integer math, 2076 clocks (20.8 microseconds) per letter, about 530 times faster than numpy on the ARM.
